summary: Verified QR cross-device login (qr/create + qr/status + qr/claim) + ABN-style PinLanding redesign + /qr-link deep-link page + existing PIN regression. Backend: 9/9 new tests pass (test_qr_cross_device.py) covering token creation, anonymous create, pending status, auth-required claim, double-claim 400, unknown token 404, and end-to-end issued access_token validates against /auth/me. Frontend: Desktop /login QR tab toggle works, renders qr-code-svg + 'Wachten op scan...' message. Mobile /surirent/login PinLanding redesign shows Welkom + GOPI APPARTEMENT + profile photo + 4-cijferige PIN prompt + 4 dots + numpad with letters + Scan QR (top-left) + Help (top-right). Help modal opens with 3 numbered steps. QR scanner modal opens and html5-qrcode shows expected 'Camera toegang geweigerd' state in headless playwright (no camera available — expected). /qr-link?token=X with auth shows confirm page, clicking 'Bevestig en log in' calls claim and shows 'Desktop ingelogd!' success state; backend status flips to 'claimed' with access_token. Existing kiosk PIN 1234 → /surirent/kiosk login still works (no regression). Fixed 1 bug: /qr-link?token=X unauthenticated redirect went to /qr-link/login instead of /login because 'qr-link' was being parsed as a company slug — added 'qr-link' + 'qr' to RESERVED_SLUGS in /app/frontend/src/lib/branded-nav.js. Re-verified: redirect now correctly goes to /login with sessionStorage.pending_qr_token preserved.
action_items: Main agent: consider also adding 'qr-link' (and any other top-level non-branded routes) to backend RESERVED_SLUGS so a company cannot register that slug. Currently only the frontend nav list was patched; the backend reservation list should mirror it for safety. Check server.py RESERVED_SLUGS constant.

Optional: in QrScannerModal, when camera permission is denied, show a fallback 'Voer code handmatig in' input — current UX only offers 'Sluiten' which is fine but a fallback would be nicer for desktops without camera.
critical_code_review_comments: qr_status endpoint correctly marks pending→expired on read; however it does not mark already-expired-but-pending sessions before checking status in qr_claim — qr_claim handles it inline (good), but the 'already claimed' check at line 1158 fires BEFORE the expiry check so a session that expired without being claimed will still return 'al gebruikt of verlopen' message; consider reversing the order so expired sessions return the more specific 'verlopen — vraag nieuwe aan' message.

qr_sessions Mongo collection lacks a TTL index on expires_at — sessions accumulate forever. Suggest creating a TTL index: db.qr_sessions.create_index('expires_at', expireAfterSeconds=600) so the collection self-cleans.

buildBrandedPath RESERVED_SLUGS list is duplicated between frontend (branded-nav.js) and backend (server.py); high risk of drift. Suggest exposing a public GET /api/_reserved_slugs endpoint that the frontend reads at startup, or move list to a shared JSON.

QrLinkPage uses sessionStorage.pending_qr_token but PasswordView/LoginPage does not appear to consume it after successful login to auto-resume the claim — main agent should verify that flow: user without auth scans QR → /qr-link → /login → logs in → expected to auto-resume claim. If not implemented, the deep-link UX has a dead-end after login.

rca of the issue: Bug: /qr-link?token=X unauthenticated redirect landed on /qr-link/login instead of /login. RCA: useBrandedNavigate() in /app/frontend/src/lib/branded-nav.js parses the first URL segment as a company slug unless it appears in RESERVED_SLUGS. 'qr-link' was missing, so the hook prefixed nav('/login') with '/qr-link' producing '/qr-link/login'. Reproduction: open /qr-link?token=anything in a fresh browser with no admin_token in localStorage. Fix: added 'qr-link' and 'qr' to the RESERVED_SLUGS set. Verified post-fix that redirect now lands on /login with sessionStorage.pending_qr_token preserved.
